children: The exclusive private-market partnership will make Takeda’s QDENGA available for pediatric and adult vaccination, with launch expected in H1 2027

Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories and Takeda Pharmaceutical Company have entered into an exclusive distribution agreement to promote and distribute Takeda’s QDENGA dengue vaccine across India’s private market for pediatric and adult vaccination, with availability expected in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory processes. The vaccine received marketing authorisation from the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) in July 2026 for people aged 4-60 years, making it the first dengue vaccine approved in India.

Under the agreement, Dr. Reddy’s will handle promotion and distribution in the private market, while Takeda will retain rights for the public market along with overall medical and brand oversight. The companies will also undertake healthcare-professional engagement and disease-awareness activities related to dengue vaccination.

The partnership comes as dengue continues to pose a public-health challenge in India. The companies said reported dengue cases have increased 11-fold over the past two decades, while nationwide surveillance has identified circulation of all four dengue virus serotypes across multiple regions. A study cited by the companies found that one in 14 patients had concurrent infection with multiple serotypes.

“As the second-largest vaccine player in India, we believe the introduction of India’s first approved dengue vaccine is an important development for the country’s healthcare landscape,” said M.V. Ramana, CEO - Global Generics, Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories. “Through our collaboration with Takeda, we look forward to making QDENGA available to eligible individuals and contributing to efforts aimed at addressing the country’s dengue burden,” he added.

Dr. Mahender Nayak, Head of Intercontinental Markets, International Business Unit, Takeda, said the partnership would support private-market access while the company continues to work towards broader dengue-prevention efforts. The vaccine has been approved in 43 countries since 2022, according to Takeda, with more than 32 million doses distributed worldwide. QDENGA is also included in the World Health Organization’s List of Prequalified Vaccines. The collaboration combines Takeda’s experience in dengue vaccine development and disease education with Dr. Reddy’s commercial and healthcare network in India.

Takeda said its longer-term dengue strategy includes supporting surveillance, awareness, vector control and community engagement. The company has also welcomed a recent Parliamentary Committee recommendation to consider dengue vaccination under India’s Universal Immunization Programme.
